title: 8085 assembly programming
subtitle: Write it, assemble it, single-step it. Every program below runs in the simulator with real opcodes, flags and T-states.

sections.title: Your first program: add two numbers
sections.body: Memory holds 25H at 2050H and 17H at 2051H. Load HL with the address, fetch the first byte into A, step to the next, add it, step on, and store. Result 3CH at 2052H (25H + 17H = 3CH). No carry, so CY = 0.

questions.prompt: Why INX H between the reads?

choices.text: To advance the memory pointer HL to the next byte.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: MOV A,M and ADD M always use the address in HL.

figures.caption: Figure 2.7.1 — add two bytes
figures.script:
var lab = create("steplab", {"name":"add","engine":"cpu8085","program":"LXI H,2050H
MOV A,M
INX H
ADD M
INX H
MOV M,A
HLT","memory":"2050=25,17","watch":"2050,2051,2052","width":600,"height":440});

sections.title: Loops and conditions
sections.body: A loop is a counter, a body and a conditional jump back. Sum 5+4+3+2+1: B counts down, A accumulates, JNZ LOOP repeats while the zero flag is clear. Result 0FH (15), and on exit Z = 1.

worked.why: Unroll the loop: A = 0, then add B = 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.

choices.text: The zero flag is 0 (last result was not zero).

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: So the loop ends when DCR makes B zero.

figures.caption: Figure 2.8.1 — sum 1 to 5
figures.note: DCR sets Z when B reaches 0; JNZ then falls through.
figures.script:
var lab = create("steplab", {"name":"loop","engine":"cpu8085","program":"MVI B,5
MVI A,0
LOOP: ADD B
DCR B
JNZ LOOP
HLT","memory":"","watch":"","width":600,"height":440});

sections.title: Comparison and branching
sections.body: CMP r compares A with r without changing A: Z = 1 if equal, CY = 1 if A < r. This program stores the larger of two numbers at 2052H: 25H vs 17H → 25H. Decision-making is always “set flags, then conditional jump”.

questions.prompt: After CMP B, when is CY = 1?

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: The internal subtraction needed a borrow.

figures.caption: Figure 2.9.1 — the larger of two
figures.note: CMP sets carry when A < B.
figures.script:
var lab = create("steplab", {"name":"max","engine":"cpu8085","program":"LDA 2050H
MOV B,A
LDA 2051H
CMP B
JNC DONE
MOV A,B
DONE: STA 2052H
HLT","memory":"2050=25,17","watch":"2050,2051,2052","width":600,"height":440});

sections.title: Arrays and table processing
sections.body: Sum four bytes at 2050H–2053H: HL points to the array, C counts four, A accumulates. Result 0AH at 2060H (1+2+3+4 = 10 = 0AH). This “pointer + counter + loop” pattern handles any block.

questions.prompt: In the array loop, what moves the pointer?

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: HL advances one byte per pass.

responses.title: It looks right at first.
responses.body: That adds the byte; it does not move HL.

figures.caption: Figure 2.10.1 — sum a table
figures.script:
var lab = create("steplab", {"name":"arr","engine":"cpu8085","program":"LXI H,2050H
MVI C,04H
MVI A,00H
NEXT: ADD M
INX H
DCR C
JNZ NEXT
STA 2060H
HLT","memory":"2050=01,02,03,04","watch":"2050,2051,2052,2053,2060","width":600,"height":440});

sections.title: BCD arithmetic and DAA
sections.body: In BCD each decimal digit occupies a nibble. Adding 38 and 45 in plain binary gives 7DH, not the BCD 83. DAA (decimal adjust accumulator) fixes it: add 6 to a nibble above 9 or with auxiliary carry. Here 38H + 45H = 7DH → DAA → 83H (= 83 decimal).

choices.text: Corrects the accumulator after a binary addition of BCD digits.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: It adds 6 to any nibble greater than 9.

figures.caption: Figure 2.11.1 — BCD addition
figures.note: Step past ADI and again past DAA.

problems.prompt: Add 99 and 01 in BCD on the 8085. What are A and CY afterwards?
problems.answer: Binary: 99H + 01H = 9AH. DAA adds 66H → 00H with a carry out: A = 00H, CY = 1 (the decimal 100).

sections.title: Subroutines and the stack
sections.body: CALL pushes the return address on the stack (SP decreases by 2) and jumps; RET pops it. Always initialise SP first (LXI SP,…). PUSH/POP save registers around a call. The stack grows downward in memory.

choices.text: Decreases by 2 (the return address is pushed).

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: The 8085 stack grows toward lower addresses.

responses.title: It looks right at first.
responses.body: The return address is stored there.

figures.caption: Figure 2.12.1 — call and return
figures.note: After CALL, SP has dropped by 2; after RET it is restored.
figures.script:
var lab = create("steplab", {"name":"call","engine":"cpu8085","program":"LXI SP,3000H
MVI A,7
CALL DBL
HLT
DBL: ADD A
RET","memory":"","watch":"","width":600,"height":440});
